questions.question: An argument is a claim supported by what?
A claim is best described as what?
choices: a position that can be supported with reasons
an example that proves every point

questions.question: Evidence is relevant when it does what?
choices: repeats the claim word for word
directly supports the claim or reason

questions.question: A school newsletter claims later start times help students and cites a local attendance study. What is the study’s role?
A writer says, “The park should add lights because visitors leave early when it gets dark.” Which part is the claim?
A counterclaim is what?
choices: a second example supporting the same reason
a fact that cannot be checked
a different position that an argument addresses

questions.question: A rebuttal responds to a counterclaim by doing what?
choices: explaining why it is limited or less convincing

questions.question: Which is the strongest evidence for a claim about local bus delays?
choices: one person’s memory of a ride years ago
a recent log of arrival times from the bus system

questions.question: A writer claims daily reading improves vocabulary, then cites a study tracking students over a semester. What makes the evidence useful?
choices: it directly relates to the claim and gives observed information
it is the writer’s favorite study
it proves every student learns identically

questions.question: A survey of ten friends is used to claim that all teenagers prefer online books. What is the main weakness?
choices: the claim is written in a sentence
the sample may be too small and unrepresentative

questions.question: A source reports that students who join a club also earn higher grades. What should an argument avoid assuming without more evidence?
choices: the two measures are related in the sample
club participation alone caused the higher grades

questions.question: A claim is supported only by examples from one unusual case. What should a reader question?
choices: whether the writer used a title
whether the claim is a sentence
whether the evidence is sufficient and representative

questions.question: Which statement is a counterclaim to “The town should build a new bike path”?
choices: A new path could connect two neighborhoods.
More residents ride bikes in summer.
The path would be near the library.
Existing streets already have safe bike lanes on most routes.

questions.question: A writer responds to the counterclaim by citing crash reports from streets without bike lanes. What is this response?
A report uses a graph showing fewer injuries after a safety rule began. What question helps assess the argument?
choices: Is the graph printed in color?
Does the report have a long title?
Could other changes also explain the decline?
Is the rule easy to spell?

questions.question: An argument includes accurate facts that do not address its claim. How should the evidence be judged?
A writer presents only examples that support a position and omits known contrary findings. What concern arises?
A claim says “every student benefits,” but evidence comes from one classroom. What adjustment would make the claim more responsible?
choices: keep the claim and remove the evidence
narrow the claim or provide broader evidence

questions.question: Which argument is best supported?
choices: “The library should extend hours; visitor counts show demand during the final hour.”
“The library should extend hours because libraries are nice.”
“Everyone agrees, so it must be right.”
“More books exist than yesterday, therefore hours should change.”

questions.question: A source finds a correlation between screen time and sleep, but cannot show which caused the other. What is a careful conclusion?
choices: screen time always causes poor sleep
the variables are associated, but causation is not established
